question.text: Two transparent media having refractive indices <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> are separated by a spherical refracting surface of radius of curvature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The centre of curvature of surface is towards denser medium and a point object is placed on the principal axis in rarer medium at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the pole of the surface. The distance of image from the pole of the surface is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Let's consider the following diagram-

The relation between the object distance, the image distance and the radius of curvature of the spherical surface can be written as

μ2v-μ1u=μ2-μ1R   ...1

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required image distance.

1.5v-1-15=1.5-1.030⇒1.5v=160-115=-120⇒v=-30

Hence, the image is formed at a distance of 30 cm from the pole on the same direction as the object is placed.
